stem: A sample of iron is analysed using a mass spectrometer. The mass spectrum shows three isotopes of iron are present in the sample.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Fig. 2.1 shows the mass spectrum of the sample of iron.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}
parts.text:
Use Fig. 2.1 to calculate the relative atomic mass, $A_{\text{r}}$, of iron to **one** decimal place.

Show your working.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Deduce the number of pairs of electrons in the shell with principal quantum number $n = 3$ in an $\text{Fe}$ atom.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Write an equation to represent the first ionisation energy of iron.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Suggest how the value for the first ionisation energy of $^{54}\text{Fe}$ compares to the first ionisation energy of $^{56}\text{Fe}$. Explain your answer in terms of the factors that affect ionisation energy.
